name: Set or Decrease
description: You are given an integer array $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ and integer $$$k$$$. In one step you can either choose some index $$$i$$$ and decrease $$$a_i$$$ by one (make $$$a_i = a_i - 1$$$); or choose two indices $$$i$$$ and $$$j$$$ and set $$$a_i$$$ equal to $$$a_j$$$ (make $$$a_i = a_j$$$). What is the minimum number of steps you need to make the sum of array $$$\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n}{a_i} \le k$$$? (You are allowed to make values of array negative).
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$) — the number of test cases. The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$1 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$; $$$1 \le k \le 10^{15}$$$) — the size of array $$$a$$$ and upper bound on its sum. The second line of each test case contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — the array itself. It's guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases doesn't exceed $$$2 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, print one integer — the minimum number of steps to make $$$\sum\limits_{i=1}^{n}{a_i} \le k$$$.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1622C — Set or Decrease [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
